answer:
Given data:
- Weight of block A, $W_A = 100\text{ N}$
- Weight of block B, $W_B = 50\text{ N}$
- Coefficient of friction for block A, $\mu_A = 0.2$
- Coefficient of friction for block B, $\mu_B = 0.5$

**Step 1: Equations of Equilibrium along the Inclined Plane**
Let $\theta$ be the inclination angle of the plane with the horizontal.
For any block on an incline of angle $\theta$:
- Normal reaction $N = W \cos\theta$
- Limiting friction force $F_f = \mu N = \mu W \cos\theta$
- Component of weight down the plane = $W \sin\theta$

When the blocks are on the verge of sliding down:
Let $T$ be the tension in the connecting rope.

For **Block A** (assuming it tends to slide down)::
$$W_A \sin\theta - T - \mu_A W_A \cos\theta = 0$$
$$100 \sin\theta - T - 0.2(100) \cos\theta = 0$$
$$100 \sin\theta - T - 20 \cos\theta = 0 \implies T = 100 \sin\theta - 20 \cos\theta \quad \text{--- (1)}$$

For **Block B** (connected by the rope parallel to the plane):
$$W_B \sin\theta + T - \mu_B W_B \cos\theta = 0$$
$$50 \sin\theta + T - 0.5(50) \cos\theta = 0$$
$$50 \sin\theta + T - 25 \cos\theta = 0 \implies T = 25 \cos\theta - 50 \sin\theta \quad \text{--- (2)}$$

**Step 2: Solve for Angle $\theta$**
Equating equations (1) and (2):
$$100 \sin\theta - 20 \cos\theta = 25 \cos\theta - 50 \sin\theta$$
$$150 \sin\theta = 45 \cos\theta$$
$$\tan\theta = \frac{45}{150} = 0.3$$
$$\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.3) = 16.7^\circ$$

**Step 3: Determine Tension $T$**
Substitute $\theta = 16.7^\circ$ into Equation (1):
$$T = 100 \sin(16.7^\circ) - 20 \cos(16.7^\circ)$$
$$T = 100(0.287) - 20(0.9576) = 28.7 - 19.15 = 9.55\text{ N}$$
proTip: Be careful with the direction of the friction force: it always opposes impending motion (up the plane if sliding down).
